title: Saltline
author: felixrieseberg
prompt: You know, you should also build me a FPS. Insanely detailed quality pls, something that looks visually like it can keep up with AAA. Make it small in scope (like a tiny level) but otherwise impressive photorealistic graphics
best_part: Photoreal container port at golden hour: wet asphalt, volumetric light, weapon model with red-dot sight, restrained objective HUD
take: Everything: it is the bar. Its prompt (recipe 01), HUD grammar, single 1.46 MB file and drag-to-look fallback

title: What the Water Keeps
author: kevin_t_ngo
best_part: Painterly golden-hour boat ride: backlit pier, mist, light shafts on water; reads like a shipped art game
take: The light: low sun, haze and warm water reflections. The structure: one slow verb (row) through a sequence of dream worlds

title: Turbo Tails kart racer
author: petergyang
best_part: Sunlit island track with lava, hot-air balloons and sailboats; animal racers; reads like a console kart game
take: The establishing fly-over and saturated holiday-island palette; how a small level is made to feel big

title: Five-style procedural 3D world
author: LexnLin
best_part: One terrain, five rendering styles on keys 1 to 5 (natural, toon, painterly and more)
take: The style switcher as a look-exploration tool: build one scene, flip looks, pick the strongest before polishing

title: Tidebreaker
author: chongdashu
best_part: Storm-at-night art direction: a waking stone giant with glowing eyes over rain-lashed pylons in a black sea
take: One huge set-piece creature as the level, and the cold-blue rain palette with warm accent lights

title: JIRA-ticket space-station horror
author: emollick
best_part: Your own work tickets become voiced audio logs in a dark space station; confident title screen
take: The personal-input premise (the player supplies the content), and the title-screen type treatment

title: Cartoon-animal capture the flag
author: chongdashu
best_part: Miniature-diorama backyard: warm light, toy-scale fences, ponds and garden beds
take: The tilt-shift toy-world look for a small arena

title: UP! with a stranger
author: ilyxxxa
best_part: Clay-plasticine characters with soft shading
take: The clay material look for characters

title: I Would Have Gotten Away With It
author: emollick
best_part: Reversed mystery (you are the culprit) in a moody illustrated manor at night
take: The reversed-role premise and the inked night-manor lighting

title: Spellwright
author: liampoli
best_part: Type any spell and the game makes it
take: The "describe it and it exists" verb, if a runtime model call is ever allowed; the look is plain

title: Skyhold
author: 0xbobaaa
best_part: A floating island that tilts under what you build; past 15 degrees it slides; a daily island the same for everyone
take: The physical-balance rule and the shared daily seed; everything drawn in code

title: 21-world boss game
author: EMostaque
best_part: Boss rush: 21 worlds, each boss a different one-tap game
take: The structure: one input, many bosses, each a new rule

title: Bottle Studio
author: AmirMushich
best_part: Studio-lit glass bottle with see-through liquid and lens bokeh in one HTML file
take: The glass, liquid and studio-light setup for hero props and pickups

title: Accra Crazy Trotro
author: Ed_Forson
best_part: A local minibus taxi game in a sunny low-poly city
take: The local-place premise; a readable bright low-poly city

title: Riposte multiplayer FPS
author: mdaman010
best_part: A finished browser FPS: classes, attachments, outfits, mobile, multiplayer; greenhouse map with real foliage
take: Read the MIT code for weapon handling, attachments and mobile controls; it uses CC0 textures and skies
licence: MIT (code only; name, logo, music, soldier animations and some sounds excluded)

title: Lakeside pixel-art fishing
author: CuriousOne_01
best_part: Isometric 3D pixel-art pond with a day clock and a fish book
take: The 3D-rendered-as-pixel-art look

title: Moss
author: BeyondTheBoxCN
best_part: A mossy floating rock with about 590,000 procedural leaves and no imported assets
take: The procedural moss and foliage instancing; MIT code

title: Code-generated rhythm game
author: blueemi99
best_part: Flat poster-illustration harbour with four seals, one per key
take: The poster look and the four-performer rhythm layout

title: Boring Forest
author: AndreiProvkin
best_part: Forest river with sparkling water, light shafts and fireflies; skipping stones
take: The water glint and forest light; a tiny verb (skip a stone) as the whole hook

title: Gather fireflies pixel-art game
author: SestinaTW
best_part: Voxel-pixel night garden with glowing lanterns and fireflies
take: The emissive glow on a pixel-art palette

title: PALLET PANIC
author: chrisjdimarco
best_part: A warehouse of stacked pallets and boxes you wreck with a forklift
take: Destructible stacked props; the warehouse set dressing next to Saltline's
